home.aboutText: iAnalyze is the AI & Data Science Club under iTeam. We bring students together to explore ideas, practice new skills, and understand what data can tell us.
home.programTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis - From Zero to Insights
home.programText: Start with your first line of Python. Learn to read, clean, explore and visualize data, then bring it all together in a small team project.
home.journeyTitle: Six weeks. A new way to see data.
home.journeyText: A practical path from the essentials to your first EDA project.
home.resourceText: iAnalyze brings students together to share ideas, ask questions, and connect with others who share their curiosity.
home.communityTitle: Bring your questions. Build with others.
home.communityText: Bring your questions, share your perspective, and connect with students who are curious about AI and data science.

about.whoText: iAnalyze is a club under iTeam at Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan.
about.parentText: iAnalyze operates under iTeam at Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan. Our focus is AI and data science within this wider student community.
about.missionText: Make the first steps in AI and data science approachable through clear explanations, hands-on practice, and learning with peers.
about.visionText: A student community that asks thoughtful questions, learns with confidence, and uses data to communicate ideas clearly.
about.objectivesText: Curiosity, open conversation, and a shared interest in AI and data science bring our community together.
about.doingText: We encourage questions, different perspectives, and mutual support in a welcoming student community.
about.communityText: There is room for beginner questions, different approaches, and shared discoveries. Working together is part of the learning experience.
about.pastText: Follow the official iTeam channels for club news and opportunities to connect with the community.

syllabus.title: Exploratory Data Analysis - From Zero to Insights
syllabus.overviewText: A practical introduction to exploratory data analysis. Begin with essential Python, then read, understand and clean data before turning it into clear charts and insights.

objectives.colab: Use Google Colab and write simple Python code.
objectives.pandas: Read data files and explore their contents with Pandas.
objectives.clean: Recognize common data problems and handle them appropriately.
objectives.patterns: Find patterns and answer simple questions with data.
objectives.present: Present findings through charts and a small practical project.

syllabus.whoText: Students curious about data analysis, including complete beginners. No previous Python experience is required.
syllabus.prerequisitesText: A laptop and a Google account are recommended for the practical work. No complicated software installation is needed.
syllabus.language: Arabic explanations with English technical terms.
syllabus.weeklyText: Open each week to see what you will explore.
syllabus.bufferText: Two optional weeks for catch-up, review, or an extra activity, depending on the program’s progress.
syllabus.outcomesTitle: What you will be able to do
syllabus.outcomesText: Work through a beginner EDA task: open a dataset, understand its structure, address common issues, create simple visualizations, and explain the findings.
syllabus.methodText: A short activity is planned for each teaching week. Published instructions appear in the Student Dashboard; submissions and feedback availability are announced separately.
syllabus.projectText: In Week 06, teams explore a simple dataset, carry out a basic analysis, create charts, and share their findings. Submission requirements and assessment details will be explained before the project begins.
syllabus.scheduleText: Six teaching weeks, 18 planned teaching hours, plus two optional buffer weeks. Start date and location will be announced later.

python1.title: Python Fundamentals I
python1.description: Get to know Google Colab and take your first steps with variables, basic operations, and approachable examples.

python2.description: Work with collections of values, simple conditions, and loops to solve everyday problems.

pandas.title: Introduction to Pandas
pandas.description: Get to know the Python library Pandas, open a dataset, understand rows and columns, and explore the file contents.

cleaning.title: Data Cleaning
cleaning.description: Spot missing values, duplicates, and common errors, and understand why data cleaning matters.

visualization.title: EDA & Data Visualization
visualization.description: Turn numbers into understandable information with simple statistics and charts.

project.title: Mini Project & Demo Day
project.description: Apply what you have learned to a simple dataset in teams and share your most meaningful findings.

simple.heroTitle: Learn AI and data science with your classmates
simple.heroText: A student club running hands-on courses and activities, taught by students, for students. It doesn't matter where you start, only that you're interested.
simple.aboutText: iAnalyze is a student club at Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan, part of iTeam, focused on AI and data science.
simple.planTeaserText: What we'll learn, when, and what you need to get started.
simple.courseText: A beginner course: six weeks, from Python basics to your first data analysis project. Taught in Arabic, with technical terms in English.
simple.whoText: Any student interested in data, even if you've never written code.
simple.needText: A laptop and a Google account. We use Google Colab, so no local installation is required for the course. You can also explore Power BI, an optional tool for analysing data and creating interactive reports and dashboards.
simple.planText: Each week: a short explanation, practice with the instructor, then a small activity.
simple.videoText: An Introduction to Data Science video that gives you a feel for the field. Not required to register.
simple.parentText: iAnalyze is one of the iTeam clubs at Al-Zaytoonah University of Jordan, focused on AI and data science.
simple.howText: We explain an idea briefly, try it together, then everyone tries it on their own. Questions are welcome any time.
simple.newsText: We post activity dates and announcements on the official iTeam accounts.

learning.toolsIntro: Five tools to help you learn, practise, and explore data. Understand each tool's purpose before getting started.
learning.courseNote: For the EDA course, use Google Colab to run Python in your browser. Installing Python, VS Code, or Power BI locally is optional.
learning.videoIntro: Two optional videos to help you explore data science and practise with Kaggle.
learning.videoHelp: Video not playing? Open it directly in Google Drive.

google-colab.description: A browser-based notebook for writing and running Python, with no local installation.
google-colab.why: This is the EDA course workspace. Write code, explore datasets, and follow practical activities in one notebook.
google-colab.requirements: A laptop, internet connection, modern browser, and Google account. Colab includes Python; no local setup is required.

steps.open: Open Google Colab using the official link above.
steps.account: Sign in with your Google account.
steps.notebook: Choose New notebook and give it a name.
steps.run: Enter the example below in a code cell. Use its run button or press Shift+Enter to connect a runtime and execute it.

google-colab.verification: The cell should display Hello, iAnalyze! below it. Save your notebook so you can return to it.

python.description: The programming language used in the EDA course, also available for your own computer.
python.why: A local installation lets you run Python outside Colab. It is optional because Colab already provides Python.
python.requirements: A supported Windows, macOS, or Linux computer and permission to install software. VS Code is a separate, optional editor.

steps.download: Open the official Python downloads page and choose a current supported Python 3 release for your operating system.
steps.windows: Windows: follow the official install-manager or installer instructions shown for your download. Complete setup, then reopen your terminal.
steps.macos: macOS: download the official .pkg installer and follow its prompts. Open a new Terminal window after installation.
steps.linux: Linux: check whether python3 is already available. Otherwise use your distribution's package manager and the official Linux instructions below; keep the system Python installation intact.

python.verification: In a terminal, run the command for your operating system below. A Python 3 version confirms installation. If the command is unavailable, consult the official platform instructions.

vscode.description: A code editor for organizing files and writing programs on your computer.
vscode.why: Use VS Code when you want a local Python workspace. It is optional for the Colab-based EDA course.
vscode.requirements: Install Python separately for local execution. Use Microsoft's Python extension. The Jupyter extension is optional for notebook work.

steps.windows: Windows: download the matching user installer from the official page, run it, and follow the setup prompts.
steps.macos: macOS: download the matching build, open it, and move Visual Studio Code to Applications.
steps.linux: Linux: choose the package for your distribution, such as .deb or .rpm, and install it with your package manager.
steps.extension: Open VS Code, open Extensions, and install the Python extension published by Microsoft.
steps.interpreter: Open the Command Palette, choose Python: Select Interpreter, and select your installed Python interpreter.
steps.run: Create hello.py, enter the example below, save the file, and choose Run Python File in Terminal.

vscode.verification: The terminal should display Hello, iAnalyze! If no interpreter is available, install Python first and select it again.

kaggle.description: An online platform for discovering datasets and working with notebooks.
kaggle.why: Find datasets for practice and explore how others analyse data. It complements the course and needs no desktop installation.
kaggle.requirements: An internet connection and browser. A Kaggle account is needed to save or run your notebooks; some datasets have additional access terms.

steps.open: Visit Kaggle using the official link above.
steps.account: Create an account or sign in to your existing account.
steps.dataset: Open Datasets, search for a topic, and read the dataset description, file preview, and usage terms.
steps.notebook: From a dataset, choose New Notebook where available, or create a notebook and attach the dataset through its data panel.

kaggle.verification: Confirm that the dataset appears in the notebook's data panel. Run a simple Python cell, such as print(1 + 1), and check that it outputs 2.

power-bi.description: A Windows desktop application for analysing data and building interactive reports and dashboards.
power-bi.why: Explore visual reporting alongside your programming work. Power BI Desktop is optional and is not a requirement of the EDA course.
power-bi.requirements: A Windows computer meeting Microsoft's current system requirements. There is no native Power BI Desktop application for macOS or Linux.

steps.download: Open the official Microsoft page and check the current Windows requirements in the instructions linked below.
steps.install: Choose the Microsoft Store option or Microsoft's direct installer, then follow the installation prompts.
steps.open: Launch Power BI Desktop after installation.
steps.import: Choose Get data, then Text/CSV or Excel. Select a small sample file you are allowed to use, review the preview, and choose Load.

power-bi.verification: Confirm the data fields appear, then add a simple chart on the report canvas. Save the report locally; publishing online is a separate step.
